pros: Good cabin quality: Cabin gets a mix of soft touch and smooth plastics, which elevates the cabin experience

pros: Light on the pocket: The strong-hybrid powertrain offers good fuel efficiency along with smooth and quick performance
Handles well: Even after being a big family SUV, it remains planted at high speeds with minimum body roll and feels stable around a corner
Premium interiors: The cabin is covered with soft touch padding and all plastics feel smooth and sturdy
cons: Less features: For its segment and positioning, the ZR-V offers less features than some Rs 20 lakh cars, and misses out on a few flashy pieces of equipment.
Limited space: While the rear seat offers good headroom and knee room, the lack of underthigh support can cause discomfort during long journeys.

Feels peppy: Good performance, rear-wheel-drive, and is effortless to drive in the city
Good features: 10.25 touchscreen, Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, connected car features, and keyless entry.
Premium inside and out: Even with a small footprint, it looks modern on the outside, and feels upmarket on the inside
Small proportions: Makes the car ideal for city use.
cons: Less practical: No boot space without folding the rear seats
Not an allrounder: Purely a city car which should not be taken on the highway
Bumpy ride: Lots of jerks and side to side movement over bad roads

variant: MG Hector Plus Savvy Pro CVT
pros: Good cabin quality: Both the plastics and soft touch materials have a smooth and consistent finish
Easy-to-drive: Both petrol and diesel engines offer a smooth drive experience.
Generous cabin space: Puts its wheelbase to good use, offering good leg space even for occupants over 6ft tall
Good feature list: Offers a massive 14-inch touchscreen, gesture control, a 360-degree camera, and ADAS Level 2 features
Comfortable Ride: Offers a good ride quality over bad roads and keeps the occupants comfortable
cons: Needs Physical Buttons: Even with the gesture controls, the large touchscreen is still not ergonomic to use on the move
Polarising Look: Design, while distinctive, may not be to everyone’s taste. Styling may be too busy for some
Incomplete Powertrain: The lack of a diesel automatic powertrain feels like a fixable miss
ADAS is limited to the top-spec trim only

pros: Premium Cabin: Gets leatherette padding everywhere and well damped buttons
Comfortable & Handles Well: Limited body roll keeps the cabin stable and helps keep everyone comfortable
Extreme Off-road Capabilities: Gets a four-wheel drive setup, three differential locks, and many off-road modes which helps it clear any obstacles.
Great Features: Comes with a 12.3-inch touchscreen, powered front seats, a panoramic sunroof, and front seat ventilation and massage function
cons: Not Exciting To Drive: While there is enough power for easy overtakes, it can feel a little slow to pick up speeds beyond 60kmph and it does not offer a thrilling performance
Needs Better Support: Due to the floor being raised, the underthigh support is compromised in all rows.
Some Missing Equipment: Could have benefitted with 2nd row seat ventilation, physical controls for headlamps, and 2nd row sunblinds.

pros: Concept car-like styling Stands out and can pull attention away from supercars
Two battery pack options with an estimated real-world range of 400-500km makes it very usable for long road trips
The strong safety suite includes well-calibrated L2 ADAS. Works well in Indian conditions
Superb infotainment experience: dual 12.3” screens and 16-speaker Harman/Kardon Audio on offer
cons: Styling is very polarising and may be too over-the-top for some in your family
Low roof and high step inside makes Ingress egress difficult for the elderly in the family
Rear seat headroom for tall users and outward visibility for short users could have been better

pros: High mileage: Returns around 15-16 kmpl in the city in regular driving conditions.
Excellent boot space. Can store an entire suitcase set along with two soft bags.
Safety package: 5-star Global NCAP crash test rating and 6 airbags as standard.
Offers feel-good features like sunroof, 360 degree camera and 9-inch touchscreen.
Ground clearance: 163mm is more than enough to drive easily over rough roads.
Comfortable ride quality: Cushioned over regular imperfections, and limits movement on sharper potholes too.
Looks distinctive: New design elements give it an identity different from the Swift.
cons: Limited headroom: Sloping roofline limits headroom for 6-footers.
Low engine refinement and performance: Feels dull with a full load and overtakes require planning.
AMT transmission: Slow and jerky on the highway, and upshifts quite early leaving less usable power.

pros: Attractive styling: Looks muscular, but also sporty with its sloping roofline.

Easy to drive in the city and stable at high speeds.

cons: Rear seat headroom: Sloping roofline limits space for tall passengers.

Misses out on a few feel-good features: sunroof, leatherette upholstery, ventilated seats.

Multiple powertrains: Offer a choice between smooth and exciting petrol engines.
Easy to drive in the city and stable at high speeds.
Covers the basics: Keyless entry, climate control, steering mounted controls, and cruise control.
190mm ground clearance boosts confidence in new drivers.
Spacious and practical cabin: Good storage spaces and space for four adults.
cons: Rear seat headroom: Sloping roofline limits space for tall passengers.
No diesel engine option — available with Venue, Nexon and Sonet.
Misses out on a few feel-good features: sunroof, leatherette upholstery, ventilated seats.

Plastic quality in some places should’ve been better, especially for the price.

pros: Easy to drive: lightweight and amateur-friendly off-roader makes off-roading easy for amateurs.
Ride comfort: Despite being a capable off-roader, offers good ride comfort in the city.
Spacious enough for four adults.
Boot space: Usable enough for airport runs, even with all the rows up.
Attention grabber: Quirky styling, upright SUV stance, compact dimensions and bright exterior hues.
cons: Engine performance: Adequate for the city, but feels underwhelming on a highway, especially with a full load.
Cabin Practicality: Lacks basics like bottle holders in the doors and no seat back pockets.

pros: Spacious cabin: Can seat six-footers back to back comfortably.
Super efficient in the city: Has a claimed fuel efficiency of up to 25.30kmpl with the petrol and 32.73km/kg with the CNG.
Enough boot space: 270-litres is enough for two cabin-sized overnighter bags and some laptop bags.
Good city performance: Feels peppy and easy to drive.
AMT transmission feels smooth as long as you drive in a relaxed manner.
cons: Design is a hit or miss: SUV stance and cladding feels try-hard.
Misses functional features like a rear view camera, day/night inside mirror and powered ORVMs.

pros: Covers all basics with cruise control, keyless entry, auto AC, powered windows and steering mounted controls.
Sporty and vibrant: Sharp styling, LED lighting and bright colours make it look youthful!
Super efficient petrol engine: Delivers around 15kmpl in the city with ease.
Good space for 4 adults: Accommodating front seats and spacious rear seats can seat 6 footers behind another.
Sorted infotainment package with 9-inch touchscreen, wireless Android Auto and Apple Carplay and 6-speaker sound system.
cons: Interior quality could be better for the price. Too much plastic and not enough smooth surfaces.
Limited performance: 3-cylinder engine, while adequate, doesn’t feel as peppy as the older 4-cylinder engine

pros: Multiple powertrain options: mild-hybrid, strong-hybrid, CNG, manual and automatic transmission options and all-wheel drive.
Ride quality: Feels comfortable and plush over regular speed breakers and bad roads alike.
Proven 5-star crash test rating with good standard safety suite.
Super efficient: Hybrid powertrain has a claimed efficiency of 28.65kmpl!
Premium features: Panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, Level-2 ADAS, 10.1-inch touchscreen and 8-speaker Infinity sound system.
New cabin design features neatly integrated ambient lighting, feels youthful.
CNG boot space: Bumper integrated CNG tanks don’t eat up into the boot space!
cons: No ADAS with strong-hybrid, CNG or manual transmission variants.
Limited headroom: Variants with a sunroof have average rear seat headroom.
Insulation: Tyre and road noise could be better controlled.
Rivals like the Kia Seltos and MG Astor feel more premium inside.

pros: Comfortable For All: Absorbs shocks with ease, settles quickly, and limits body roll to keep all passengers comfortable.
Easy to drive: Small footprint, light steering, and light clutch make for a beginner-friendly package
Good Space and Packaging: Sliding and reclining second row, a removable third row, and tumble-fold seats give it good space and flexibility only a few cars have at this price point.
Covers All The Basics: For a 7-seater priced less than some small hatchbacks, the Gravite covers all the essentials, including a good infotainment package.
cons: Modest powertrain: The sole 1-litre NA petrol engine offers average performance levels, and the low engine refinement can be irritating. Gravite is best driven in a relaxed manner.
Feature misses: Equipment like auto climate control, a better quality rear view camera, and alloy wheels are sorely missed.

pros: Smooth drives: It has one of the best performing CVTs under Rs 10 lakh

pros: Great practicality: Adjustable front cupholders, big door pockets with a dustbin and umbrella slots, dual gloveboxes, rear removable storage box ensure more than adequate storage spaces.
Rich and ergonomic cabin: Leatherette dashboard, door pads, and steering wheel feel premium, and multiple physical dials help usability.
Premium Features: Massaging and ventilated seats with memory function, 13-speaker Canton audio system, dual wireless phone chargers and three-zone climate control.
Great highway cruiser: Sits at triple-digit speeds effortlessly with enough performance for overtakes.
cons: Squeaking sounds from a few panels inside after covering 20,000 km+.
Third row space: Only adequate for kids or pets.

pros: 446-litre boot space is more than sufficient for 4 cabin-sized trolley bags.
Enough features: Sunroof, ventilated and powered front seats, 10.1-inch touchscreen.
Fun-to-drive: 1-litre TSI engine is fun to push hard and puts a smile on your face.
Practical. Ample space for four 6-footers. Cabin storage is very well thought out too.
cons: No diesel or CNG options available.
Minor annoyances: poor camera quality, very light horn, and noisy seat ventilation blowers spoil the experience.
Fuel efficiency isn’t great, particularly in heavy city traffic. Expect 10kmpl at best.

pros: Handles like a sports car: The steering is direct and progressive while the chassis feels like it can take on more
Sleeper design: Doesn’t look overly aggressive, but is immediately recognizable to the people who know
Performance: Smooth and easy in the city, but quick and exciting when you want to have fun
Super practical: Has enough storage spaces inside the cabin and a big boot for a long vacation
cons: Sound: Engine and exhaust sound a little muted for a performance-oriented car
Rear seats: Adequate space, but the limited sense of space makes it feel claustrophobic
Ride quality: Can be too stiff for our broken roads
Ingress egress is super inconvenient with a low roof that requires you to duck a lot.

pros: Sharp looking - the redesigned grille, flush-fitting door handles, and connected tail lights give it a clean and modern look.
No compromise safety - 6 standard airbags, 360-degree camera, and an already established 5-star safety rating makes it a safe option.
Great rear seat experience - raised under thigh support and ample legroom offers great space for two average sized adults.
Only diesel engine option in the segment makes it more appealing to buyers who prioritize fuel efficiency.
Feature rich - 10.25-inch touchscreen, 10.25-inch digital driver’s display, and an electric sunroof make it a well-equipped hatchback.
cons: No diesel automatic option on sale and the diesel is limited to the one-below-top variant.
Petrol engine gets too noisy under load and has more vibrations than expected.
Turbo-petrol engine not offered with the facelifted version.
Fit and finish - many panel gaps on the outside and some flimsy elements inside break the cabin quality’s consistency.

variant: Tiago EV Creative Plus 24 Long Range
pros: Comfortable ride: Rides well over bad roads and feels stable at high speeds.
New-driver friendly: Height adjustable seats and super gentle throttle modulation make it easy to drive.
Impressive features: 10.25-inch infotainment, 360-degree camera, auto AC with rear AC vents and many other functional features are impressive for a budget car.
Battery warranty: Bigger battery gets a 15 year warranty which offers peace of mind.
Looks and feels premium: Contemporary looks and material choices inside make it feel more expensive than it is.
cons: Fit and finish: Panel gaps and inconsistent plastic panels take away from the premium experience.
No paddle shifters: Regenerative mode has to be changed via the buttons on the central console which doesn’t feel intuitive.
Boot space: Limited space in the boot is only enough for two cabin sized trolleys and a laptop bag.

pros: Usable range: 170-220 km of realistic range makes it a solid city commuter
Covers all functional equipment: Electric ORVMs, cruise control, power windows, and auto AC
Comfortable ride quality: soaks up undulations and speed breakers really well
City performance: Electric performance offers immediate acceleration and quick overtakes in the city
8-speaker sound system offers a good music experience
cons: Only packs dual airbags, even in the top-spec variant
Looks: Both exterior and interior have started to feel dated. Limited (3) exterior colour options don’t help its case either
Silly feature omissions: alloy wheels, rear AC vents, rear-adjustable headrests
Range / battery percentage read-outs could’ve been calibrated for more accuracy
Paddle shifters for changing regen modes would be more intuitive than using the button on the dashboard
Outdated infotainment package: 7-inch touchscreen feels old to use with slow response times and wired Android Auto and Apple CarPlay connectivity

pros: Big cabin upgrade: A completely redesigned, chunky dashboard and a far more comfortable, big-person-friendly driving position.
Effortless engine: The proven 2.8-litre diesel is torquey and relaxed, now paired with a smoother, more polished automatic.
Serious off-road hardware: Ladder-frame chassis, low-range 4x4, rear diff lock and a full suite of traction electronics.
Improved ride comfort: Toyota has taken a good amount of sharpness out of the ride, most noticeably in the front row.
Modern, imposing design: The redesigned face and brawnier stance look fresher and more aggressive without losing the Hilux's tough character.
cons: Still firm over big hits: Sharp speed breakers and deep potholes still send a strong jolt through the cabin.
Bulky in the city: Heavy low-speed steering and a 5,325 mm length make tight traffic and parking a chore.
Compromised rear seat: An upright, non-reclining backrest, a high floor and no rear AC vents make the back bench a poor place for family.
Under-equipped for the price: Manual AC, a manual-dimming mirror, fabric seats and no ADAS on a truck costing around Rs 35-40 lakh on-road.

pros: Interior quality: Smooth and textured plastic along with solid buttons and stalks feel rich to interact with
Design: Sharp front styling is based on Toyota’s global lineup
Good feature package: Dual digital screens, 10-way powered driver seat, ventilated front seats and ADAS.
Smooth performance: Throttle and regenerative braking calibration is super smooth
cons: Rear seat experience: Underthigh support is poor even for average-sized adults and limited sense of space
Regenerative braking: No physical button or paddle shifters means level of regen braking can only be changed when stationary
Ride quality: Comfortable at low speeds but gets bouncy and doesn’t feel settled even at 60-70kmph
360-degree camera: Quality is too grainy and not acceptable at this price
Boot space: Shallow and short boot means limited space to store big bags

variant: G Opt Aero Black Edition HYBRID

pros: Sophisticated look: Classy, understated styling. Sporty GT variant on offer too
Feature-loaded: 8-inch digital driver’s display, 10.1-inch touchscreen, ventilated seats, electric sunroof are among the highlights
Great boot space: 521 litre boot is segment leading. 60:40 split rear seats bumps up practicality
Strong engine options: 1- and 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engines promise excitement
cons: Limited powertrains: No diesel of hybrid engine options. City offers a strong hybrid powertrain.
Less rear seat space: Lack of width and strong seat contouring means the Virtus is best used as a four seater
